at2.bio: ATM — Andrelita T. Myril — is a painter and visual artist, a graduate of ENARTS, Haiti's most renowned National School of Arts. Her mission: put the tools of art in everyone's hands — to grow each person's creativity, give the mind the escape it needs, and nurture human and mental balance. Her canvases — bold colors, moving rhythms, figures and abstractions — are windows onto the light of Haiti and the Caribbean.

bia.a1_d: Hand the machine what it does well and safely: drafts, summaries, sorting, extraction, translation, file preparation. A task is only delegated once it is understood and measured.
bia.a2_d: Control what it does imperfectly: who validates, at what moment, against which criteria. Every action traced, every output tested — quality becomes provable, not promised.
bia.a3_d: Name the tasks that must stay human — judgement, client relationships, decisions, responsibility — and reinvest the saved time there. That is what makes the project last.
bia.aka: Atmart advisory for companies and NGOs
bia.aka_s: automate · supervise · strengthen the human side
bia.dl1_d: Every task in scope, its volume, its risk, and the decision: delegate, supervise, keep human.
bia.dl2_d: Real cases with the expected answer: you can measure the tool's quality today and again in six months.
bia.dl3_d: A readable log of what the tool did, with which data, and who approved it.
bia.dl4_d: Cost per task and per month, spending caps, and the threshold beyond which automation stops paying off.
bia.dl5_d: What to do when the tool is wrong, breaks down or costs too much — written for your team, not for engineers.
bia.dl6_d: What must never enter an AI tool, who is allowed to approve, and how the people concerned are informed.
bia.dl_d: Deliverables that stay with you and keep working even if you change provider.
bia.end_d: Thirty minutes, no commitment: you describe your work, we tell you where AI can help in your case — and where it should stay out.
bia.eth1: Data literacy. I publish free tutorials — in Haitian Creole, French, English and Spanish — that teach how to read a figure, spot a bias and check a source. Training your teams is part of the job, not an after-sales extra.
bia.eth2: Ethics. A badly defined indicator steers a decision that affects real people. I name the biases, I document the limits, and I refuse conclusions the data does not support — including when they would suit everybody.
bia.eth3: Privacy. Personal data minimised, anonymised, explicit consent. In the recruiting portal I built, a candidate's contact stays hidden until they are selected, and nationality never appears in a browsing list — because the law and human dignity both require it.
bia.fq1_a: That is not the goal, and it is not what we sell. We look for the repetitive tasks that wear your teams out, and we explicitly protect those that require judgement and relationships. An honest diagnostic always states what must NOT be automated.
bia.fq2_a: We sign a confidentiality agreement before any access. The diagnostic sets a written rule on what must never enter an AI tool, and the pilot is designed to work with reduced or anonymised data wherever possible.
bia.fq3_a: That is a real risk and we put it in writing. Every automation ships with its known cost, a spending cap, and a documented manual fallback. You must never be locked in by a provider.
bia.fq3_q: What if the AI provider changes its prices or rules?
bia.fq4_a: Yes — and that is where the effect is strongest: one person recovering five hours a week, in a team of six, is visible. The diagnostic is fixed-price precisely to stay affordable.
bia.fq4_q: We are a small organisation. Is this for us?
bia.fq5_a: Two pilots in parallel, at most. We prefer to say so and keep an honest schedule rather than promise deadlines that quality could not survive.
bia.hw1: A 30-minute call. You describe your work, we say plainly whether AI can help — and if the answer is no, we say that too.
bia.hw2: Diagnostic. Interviews with your teams, observation of the real work, measurement of volumes. No technical decision at this stage.
bia.hw3: Findings workshop. Ninety minutes: the task map, the roadmap, the risks. You decide whether to continue, or you stop there.
bia.hw4: Pilot. A single task, taken through to live use, with your teams in the loop.
bia.hw5: Handover. Your team runs the tool without us. That is the success criterion — not our permanent presence.
bia.kicker: You want to use AI without betting your reputation on it.
bia.lead: Most AI engagements stop at the demo that impresses in a meeting. We don't deliver a demo, we deliver proof: an automation actually in service, traceable, tested, with a known cost — and a clear list of the tasks that must stay human.
bia.lv_d: We always start small: a fixed-price diagnostic, with no obligation to continue.
bia.me2_d: That combination is rare, and it is what makes the difference on an AI project. Most monitoring-and-evaluation specialists do not build the tools they ask for; most developers have never had to defend an indicator in front of a donor. I have done both — which is why I know where automation holds, and where it breaks.
bia.me2_d2: In practice: you will get neither a consultant discovering your sector, nor a developer ignoring your obligations. You will get someone who has filled in the same reports as you, who knows what a donor checks, and who can build the tool the day the analysis says it should be built.
bia.me2_lead: Jean Wisner Myril, founder of Atmart LLC — more than 20 years in the field, four professions that answer each other: monitoring, evaluation & learning · data analysis · data engineering · development.
bia.me_d: The same compass we teach for free on Lojik360 — applied to your organisation, task by task.

bia.n2_l4: A test set that proves quality before and after

bia.of_d: We are opening this practice: the first two organisations get a launch rate in exchange for honest feedback and permission to cite the case (figures anonymised if you prefer). You gain on price, we gain the reference.
bia.pb1_d: The prototype works on three hand-picked examples. At the first unusual case nobody knows what to do, and the team goes back to its old method.
bia.pb1_t: The demo doesn't survive real work
bia.pb2_d: With no record of actions and decisions, you cannot fix an error, answer an audit, or simply trust the thing.
bia.pb2_t: Nobody can say what the tool did
bia.pb3_d: Judgement, relationships, responsibility: automated carelessly, they cost you customers, staff, and sometimes a reputation.
bia.pb_d: Three causes, always the same — and none of them is technical.
bia.pb_t: Why AI projects fail inside companies
bia.pil1_d: Logframes, indicators, field data collection (Kobo, XLSForm), data-quality control against explicit criteria, donor reports. Twenty years producing these documents — and training the teams who fill them in.
bia.pil2_d: Management dashboards (Power BI), quantitative and qualitative analysis. Turning incomplete field data into decisions you can defend in front of a board or a donor.
bia.pil3_d: Cleaning, modelling, de-duplication, documented and reusable datasets — up to complete national geographic reference files, ready for analysis.
bia.pil4_d: Applications in production, not mock-ups: multilingual AI coaches, a recruiting portal with a privacy model, a training-document generator — designed, secured and deployed.
bia.scope: 💡 The prices shown apply to a micro-organisation — up to 25 employees. Beyond that, scope and the number of teams change the workload: we issue a quote after scoping, using the same method.

bia.vid2_d: One single task taken all the way: written criteria, human control, tests, measurement. The AI never signs.
bia.vid3_d: Month 3: tests replayed, drift caught and fixed, one new use case, the team growing its skills.

bia.vid_note: ⚠️ These are teaching simulations, not results from a real client: the tasks and orders of magnitude are representative of the sector and constitute no quantified promise.

cm.bb_h: A backbone, not a file warehouse
cm.bb_note: The territory reference set is published: 11,707 entities, from department down to locality, arrondissements included. See the Backbone and its method →
cm.bb_sub: What is truly missing in Haiti is not the data: it is common identifiers. Without a shared key, a school, a market, a clinic, a price and a budget cannot be tied to the same commune or the same period. The Backbone is that foundation — and every new dataset that connects to it increases the value of all the previous ones.
cm.bes1_h: I am looking for a figure on a commune
cm.bes1_p: Open a territory's profile and read its indicators: each one carries its source, its reference year and its limitation. What is missing is written as missing, never replaced by a zero.
cm.bes2_h: I need a file to download
cm.bes2_p: Datasets ready to open in Excel, Power BI or R, delivered with their documentation: sources, variable dictionary, known limitations and licence. No account to create.

cm.bes3_p: Tell us which decision you have to make. We build the dataset to order, or we get it funded so that it becomes public — and free for everyone.

cm.ct_p: A precise need, a territory, a deadline: we reply by stating what already exists, what is being prepared, and what it would cost to build it. Answer within 48 working hours.

cm.pb1_p: Sources are scattered across institutions, donors, portals and PDFs. Nobody holds them together.
cm.pb2_p: Commune names, units, years, codes: nothing joins without being harmonized by hand.
cm.pb3_p: Where does the figure come from? How old is it? What does it not cover? Without an answer, it is indefensible.
cm.pb4_p: Two to three days of preparation per series. That cost is what we remove — not the figures, which are often public.
cm.pb_h: In our markets, the data exists. It is using it that costs.
cm.pb_sub: The raw figure is rarely the real obstacle. What blocks you is the time lost between the source and the decision. That interval is exactly what Atmart Data works on.

cm.pgm2_p: A bank, an NGO, a ministry or a foundation funds the opening of a dataset — which then becomes accessible to a whole cohort of students or researchers.
cm.pgm3_p: Recurring, public products on high-utility themes: market prices, territories, employment, financial inclusion. First observatory targeted for 2027.

cm.rd1: Phase 1 — lay the backbone (0–6 months). Territory reference set stabilized ✓, time and indicator reference sets, data-sheet standards and versioning rules, source register and legal matrix ✓, academic access framework ✓, sponsorable offers ✓.
cm.rd2: Phase 2 — the pillar products (6–12 months). Profile of the 140 communes, first geocoded school register, first versioned health register, monthly market panel, harmonized macro-financial base, first licences and first sponsorships.
cm.rd3: Phase 3 — industrialize, and only then extend (12–24 months). Multi-source cross-referencing, access to services, sector packs, university agreements. Replicating the method to the Caribbean and then to Francophone Africa only begins after the first year, once Haiti is covered.
cm.rd_note: The order is not decorative: publishing a school register before stabilizing the territory means condemning yourself to redo it. The portfolio in 5 layers →
cm.rd_sub: Regional expansion is not a diversification: it is the replication of a method already proven on difficult ground.
cm.rep_note: Every figure is extracted from an official PDF sealed by a SHA-256 hash, with its internal checks (sum of the months, execution rate). Download the national benchmark CSV — documented columns: concept, period, source, document hash, limitations.
cm.rep_p1: authorized spending executed over 9 months — 51.75% of the revised budget of 360.3 bn
cm.rep_p2: per inhabitant over these 9 months (population: 2024 UNFPA projection — an order of magnitude, not a measurement)
cm.rep_p3: actual disbursements according to the TOFE (cash basis) — a different reference frame; the gap is normal and documented
cm.rep_sub: The Ministry of Economy and Finance publishes budget execution on budget.gouv.ht — but only at the national level, ministry by ministry: no breakdown by commune or department exists to date. Here, then, is what can honestly be published, taken from the official documents of the ongoing 2025-2026 fiscal year (cumulative from 1 October 2025 to 30 June 2026, that is 9 months out of 12).
cm.tr_p1: We apply a simple rule, to ourselves included: we only put on sale what we can deliver today. The catalogue therefore shows three states — Available Sponsorable In preparation — and never a "Buy" button on a file that does not exist yet.
cm.tr_p2: As of 14 August 2026: 5 datasets on sale, 23 free resources — including the four master reference sets of the Backbone and the source register — and 5 datasets in preparation, open to sponsorship. All of them cover Haiti: regional and African datasets are withdrawn from the catalogue until the second year.

ds.b_pack: See what the pack brings together
ds.c10_p: Rice, beans, oil, fuel: price readings by market and by month, 2018–2025. Sources: CNSA, FEWS NET.
ds.c11_meta: 🗺 Geography • Extract from the Haiti Geo Pack
ds.c11_p: Ten communal sections with their French and Haitian Creole names, OCHA p-codes, area and GPS coordinates: exactly the structure of the Geo Pack, so you can judge before buying.
ds.c12_meta: 👥 Social • United States (MA) • v2026.07 • Public professional contact details — usage rules
ds.c12_p: 517 districts with the leadership contact: name, role, work email, phone, town and county. Compiled from the state's public directories, deduplicated and verified. For legitimate B2B outreach — training, school transport, education services.
ds.c13_h: Haiti territorial reference set — base NEW
ds.c13_meta: 🗺 Geography • Open layer of the Backbone • Source: CNIGS via OCHA
ds.c13_p: Haiti's 10 departments, 42 arrondissements and 140 communes with a stable Atmart identifier, OCHA p-code, French and Haitian Creole names, chief town, area and coordinates. The join key to drop into your own databases.
ds.c14_p: For every source we use: organisation, URL, licence, legal class, coverage, frequency and last verification date. What we are allowed to publish, and what we are not.
ds.c15_meta: 📅 Time • 2nd master reference set of the Backbone • date table ready for Power BI
ds.c15_p: 1,201 periods from 1971 to 2030: annual, half-year, quarterly, monthly — and the Haitian fiscal year, running 1 October to 30 September. Every month knows its quarter, its budget year and its freshness status. Labels in French and Haitian Creole.
ds.c16_meta: 📊 4th master reference set of the Backbone • 1,251 values declared unavailable rather than set to zero
ds.c16_p: 2,949 values computed across the 140 communes: area, sections, localities, population, population density, health facilities, schools, markets and an administrative completeness score. Ships with its dictionary: calculation method, comparability, limitations and reading guidance for each of the 32 defined indicators.
ds.c17_h: Age pyramid of the 140 communes NEW
ds.c17_meta: 👥 Population • 17 brackets × 2 sexes × 140 communes • Source: UNFPA 2024 projections
ds.c17_p: The population of each commune by five-year bracket and by sex. This is what makes it possible to say how many school-age children or elderly people live in a territory — and no longer just how many inhabitants. These are projections, not a census: Haiti's last census dates from 2003.
ds.c18_meta: 💰 Economy • Source: WFP — VAM Food Prices • the series can also be read in the Explorer
ds.c18_p: Monthly price readings, product by product and market by market: rice, beans, maize, oil, fuel. The network does not cover the whole country — 9 sentinel markets, one per department in nine departments out of ten. To be read as a signal, never as a national average.
ds.c19_p: The recorded markets: stable identifier, normalised name, attachment to the communal section and coordinates. This is the family whose coverage holds — 136 communes out of 140, and every record is geolocated.
ds.c1_meta: 📘 Teaching guide • ideal for trainers, schools & workshops • preview: the free tutorial
ds.c1_p: The full Lojik360 University module: 6 modules (foundations, arguments, evidence, bias, problem-solving, practice) with exercises, a capstone, a grading rubric and reflection prompts. In French, Creole, English and Spanish (4 Word files).
ds.c20_meta: 🏛 Public finance • 2025-2026 financial year • Sources: MEF / Direction Générale du Budget, TOFE
ds.c20_p: Public spending actually executed at national level, for the current financial year, drawn from citable official documents. Two markers only, and that is deliberate: there is no breakdown by department or by commune, because the source does not publish one. Two sourced figures are worth more than an invented distribution.
ds.c21_h: Presence of organisations — who works where NEW
ds.c21_p: Which organisations work in which commune, and in which sector. These are presences declared by the organisations themselves to OCHA's 3W, not a field survey: an absence from this file does not prove an absence on the ground.
ds.c22_meta: 🤝 Infrastructure • Source: MPCE — official NGO register
ds.c22_p: Non-governmental organisations recognised by the State: registration number, date of recognition, field of work and declared areas. The contact details are institutional — those of the head office, not of individuals.
ds.c23_h: Legal and land professions by commune NEW
ds.c23_meta: ⚖️ Infrastructure • Trust level C • compiled sources, outside the official register
ds.c23_p: How many notaries and land surveyors are recorded in each commune. The count alone: no name, no address, no telephone. A zero means "none in our sources", never "none in the territory" — 55 communes out of 140 are covered.
ds.c24_meta: 🏗 Infrastructure • vintage and source declared row by row
ds.c24_p: What each commune has in facilities, family by family. One row per commune and per type, with its source and its vintage — enough to compare territories without confusing what is counted with what is estimated.
ds.c25_meta: 🏫 Social • Sources: MENFP, OCHA • trust level C
ds.c25_p: 4,117 schools, public and non-public, attached to their commune. Partial coverage, and we say so: 49 communes out of 140, and no GPS coordinates. The price takes account of that.
ds.c26_meta: 🏥 Social • Sources: MSPP, OCHA • trust level C
ds.c26_p: 730 facilities — hospitals, centres, dispensaries — attached to their communal section, of which 480 are geolocated. Coverage of 14 communes out of 140: that is little, it is written down, and the price reflects it.
ds.c27_meta: 🗺 Geography • Source: CNIGS via OCHA; GeoNames
ds.c27_p: The part of the Geo Pack that concerns one department: communal sections, chief town, populated places and polygons. For anyone working on a single territory. The whole country remains the better deal — ten separate departments cost $90, the full pack $29.
ds.c28_meta: 📦 Cross-cutting • Sources: CNIGS via OCHA, GeoNames, MENFP, MSPP
ds.c28_p: The full Geo Pack, the school register and the health facility register, together. $59 instead of $63 bought separately. The partial coverage of the two registers remains what it is — 49 and 14 communes out of 140 — and that is written on their page.
ds.c29_h: Workbook of the 140 communal profiles NEW
ds.c29_meta: 📊 Cross-cutting • assembly of the published datasets • CC BY 4.0 licence for the data

pg.backbone.lead: Republishing a public file helps nobody. What Haiti lacks is shared identifiers: enough to link a school, a market, a clinic, a price and a budget to the same commune, the same reference population and the same period. The Backbone is that base. Every new dataset attaches to it — and raises the value of all the others.

xp.box_h3: What this explorer does — and what it does not
xp.box_p1: It shows the information currently documented by Atmart Data — not everything that exists about a commune. Everything runs in your browser: four public files and one map outline, no application server, no account, no advertising tracker. An anonymous and aggregated audience measurement counts uses (a search happened) without ever knowing who or what — no cookie, no identifier, no IP address kept, and the text you type never leaves your browser: full method. What you see, you can download as is from the catalogue and recompute yourself.
xp.box_p2: The commune is the most detailed territorial level of the public edition. Communal sections, populated places and detailed polygons are available in the Haiti Geo Pack. Definitions, methods and quality statuses are set out on the Backbone page.
xp.class_note: Departments and arrondissements have no values of their own: they are aggregated from their communes according to the rule written in the dictionary, and the number of documented communes is shown alongside. The + button adds a territory to the comparison.
xp.comp_note: Two to four territories side by side — communes, arrondissements or departments. Every value carries its reference year, and comparisons across different years are flagged rather than smoothed over.

xp.lead: Search a commune, an arrondissement or a department, and read its profile: essential services, available indicators, sources and reference years. Compare territories, spot service gaps and export the results for your reports, projects and decisions.
xp.mil_l1: 2003 census (IHSI) — the last exhaustive demographic base.
xp.mil_l2: CNIGS / OCHA COD-AB — the administrative division valid as at 29 November 2018, republished on 26 January 2026. This is the one this explorer uses for this edition, because it is the only one providing official join codes and geometries. Used does not mean in force today : communes have been created since.
xp.mil_l3: Recent IHSI demographic estimates — they include communes created after 2018 and therefore show higher totals.
xp.mil_p1: Haiti does not have a single territorial reference set, but several vintages that coexist:
xp.mil_p2: Exact wording: this version of the Explorer covers the 140 communes of the 2018 CNIGS reference set. More recent vintages recognise additional communes. A territory absent from 2018 is not a territory that does not exist — it is absent from that vintage.
xp.mil_p3: For the Ouest department: the 2018 CNIGS reference set contains 20 communes. This number may differ in more recent reference sets. We obtained it by counting this file, not by taking it from a third party.
xp.mil_p4: The vintage correspondence table (CSV, 192 entities) gives, for each territory, its Atmart identifier, its p-code, its vintage, its validity dates and a divergence note. Today it holds only the 2018 vintage: the others will be added when we have the official files, not before.
xp.mil_p5: We do not pick a number in silence: the explorer counts what the reference set it loads actually contains, and names it. Communes created after 2018 will be added with their validity dates as soon as an official reference set publishes them with their codes, without rewriting history.
